generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport, a lot of learning by doing happens in placements and practical work. A sport and exercise science student might spend time in a human performance lab, testing athletes and handling real data under supervision. The school also sets work-like tasks inside its courses, such as running a fitness assessment or a training study, where you learn the craft of your subject by doing it rather than only reading about it.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two School of Sport students, both told their sport and exercise science module includes a placement in a human performance lab.

Tom treats the lab placement as time away from real study. He turns up, follows the testing protocol, and waits to be told what to do, expecting the real learning to happen later, back in lectures. The sessions pass and the data gets collected, but Tom does not see the placement itself as learning.

Amara treats the placement as the learning. She runs real tests on athletes, watches how experienced physiologists read the results, and notices what the lab teaches that a textbook cannot. The work is not a break from study; it is a different way of studying sport and exercise science, through doing.

Both students did the same placement. Only Amara recognised it as practice- and work-based learning: learning that comes from taking part in real work.
generatedProse.summary: Practice- and work-based learning in the School of Sport is learning by doing: taking part in real tasks in a lab, clinic, club or work-like project, rather than only studying them from the outside. You can now explain what it is and recognise it in a sport student's experience. The next lesson looks at the many forms it takes across the school's subjects.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's lab placement practice- and work-based learning?

items.text: She took part in real testing and treated the experience itself as learning.
She waited until she was back in lectures to do the real learning.
She spent longer in the lab than Tom did.
She read more about the testing protocol before she started.

feedback.correct: That's right. Taking part in real testing and learning from the experience is what makes it practice- and work-based learning.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara DID, beyond turning up or reading.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's placement was practice- and work-based learning because she took part in real testing and learned from the experience itself.
